CHAPTER 22
 
Nu 22:1-20. Balak's First Message for Balaam Refused.

1. Israel ... pitched in the plains of Moab--so called from having formerly belonged to that people, though wrested from them by Sihon. It was a dry, sunken, desert region on the east of the Jordan valley, opposite Jericho.

Come ... curse me this people--</hi>Among the heathen an opinion prevailed that prayers for evil or curses would be heard by the unseen powers as well as prayers for good, when offered by a prophet or priest and accompanied by the use of certain rites. Many examples are found in the histories of the Greeks and Romans of whole armies being devoted to destruction, and they occur among the natives of India and other heathen countries still. In the Burmese war, magicians were employed to curse the British troops. <div eID="gen2000" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1494"/><div sID="gen2004" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1494"/><hi type="bold">19-20. tarry ye also here this night, that I may know what the Lord will say unto me more--</hi>The divine will, as formerly declared, not being according to his desires, he hoped by a second request to bend it, as he had already bent his own conscience, to his ruling passions of pride and covetousness. The permission granted to Balaam is in accordance with the ordinary procedure of Providence. entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1498"/><div sID="gen2008" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1498"/><hi type="bold">28. the Lord opened the mouth of the ass--</hi>to utter, like a parrot, articulate sounds, without understanding them. That this was a visionary scene is a notion which seems inadmissible, because of the improbability of a vision being described as an actual occurrence in the middle of a plain history. Besides, the opening of the ass's mouth must have been an external act, and that, with the manifest tenor of Peter's language, strongly favors the literal view [2Pe 2:15, 16]. The absence of any surprise at such a phenomenon on the part of Balaam may be accounted for by his mind being wholly engrossed with the prospect of gain, which produced "the madness of the prophet" [2Pe 2:16]. "It was a miracle, wrought to humble his proud heart, which had to be first subjected in the school of an ass before he was brought to attend to the voice of God speaking by the angel" [Calvin]. <div eID="gen2008" type="x-p"/>
